content: The classification of diabetes, as defined by the American Diabetes Association (ADA), includes the following categories: 1. Type 1 Diabetes: This form of diabetes is caused by autoimmune destruction of pancreatic β-cells. This destruction typically results in an absolute deficiency of insulin production, meaning the body is unable to produce insulin on its own. 2. Type 2 Diabetes: This type is frequently associated with insulin resistance, where the body's cells do not respond effectively to insulin. Over time, it is also characterized by a progressive decline in the ability of the pancreas to secrete insulin adequately. 3. Other Specific Types of Diabetes: These include less common forms of diabetes such as neonatal diabetes, which occurs in newborns, and maturity-onset diabetes of the young (MODY), which is a monogenic form of diabetes that typically presents in adolescence or early adulthood. Additionally, diabetes can result from pancreatic diseases or as a side effect of certain medications.
